utterances.text: The conditions were terrible, frightening. I couldn't change the baby's diapers. I poured water. I gave the baby water just to keep it alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Could you use toilet facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes, if the HVO soldiers gave us permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, how were the -- how were you and the others treated? Let's first say, for how long did you stay at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Two days and two nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And how were you treated by the soldiers during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: As they wished.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Were people mistreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to your sister -- your sister-in-law? Maybe without mentioning her name since ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: She was taken out on a number of occasions, beaten up. They would bring her back into the room in semiconscious condition, telling her that whatever she had seen and heard that she should keep to herself; otherwise, she would get killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Was she taken, just taken out on one occasion or more, on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And do you know who took her out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Velimir Dojcinovic, also known as Vela.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: So now you said you stayed there for two days. What happened -- so that brings us to the 22nd of April. Where were you taken on the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: On the 22nd of April at about 11.00 in the morning, a car came for our group. We were boarded into that vehicle, and we went towards Kraj or Junuzovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: I now am going to show you a photograph which I would like you to look at, and that will be exhibit number 6.30. Can you see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Which houses --

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. Is it 6.30 or 6.13? I was going to correct the interpreter, but I think they were right. It is 6.13?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, one three, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One three, yes. Because in the transcript we see 6.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fourmy.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness D, so do you recognise these houses as the Junuzovic houses -- Junuzovici houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: What I would like you to do is take the red marker, which you're going to get from the usher, and indicate on the photograph, maybe by putting a circle around the house where you stayed, where you in fact were brought on that day, on the 22nd of April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I see you've circled a house without a roof. At the time you were taken there, did the house have a roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And all the other houses on that photograph who are without roofs also had roofs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: So the whole group of women, elderly men, and children, the 540 -- all 540 were all moved to the Junuzovici houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And over how many houses were -- was this group then divided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Six houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And do you recall with how many people you stayed in the house you were put in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: There was 13 of us in a room three by three.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And how many rooms did the house have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, while you were at the Junuzovici houses, or Junuzovici house, how were you treated there? Was your house -- was your house guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes. All the houses were guarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: So you were not able to go out of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: No, we couldn't go out. But they could come in whenever they wanted to. We didn't -- we were not allowed to keep the door locked.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And when you said "they could come in," you're referring to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And why would they come in? What would they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: They would take girls out.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: So at the house where you stayed, girls were taken out on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And would these girls later on be brought back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And what do you think would have happened with them? When they would be coming back, how would they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Far from nice.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Would they have bruises or were they maltreated? Could you see anything on their body or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to you at one moment in the period that you were staying at the Junuzovici house. At one moment you overheard a conversation between some soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what those soldiers were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: They were saying all kinds of things, that they should all be killed, that they should all be forced out, lined up against a wall, executed. Terrible things they were saying. It's hard to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Did they refer to the name Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: What did they say about Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: In answer to our questions as to why all this was happening, what was the reason, was it only because we were Muslims, then we would get a simple answer, "Tuta's orders."

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, at what time did you leave the Junuzovici houses, what date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: On the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And what happened on the 4th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: On the 4th of May, they called us out on a loudspeaker. They told us to come out. They informed us to pack our things and to wait for buses which would come to pick us up and that we would be transported to the Sovicka gates, Sovicka Vrata.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: So how many buses were there to pick you up from the Junuzovici houses? How many buses or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: There were two buses and a truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And did these two buses and the truck take all 540 people straight to Sovicka Vrata?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: No. No. Thirty people boarded one bus, 30 people at a time. The others would wait until that group was transported and then the buses would come back to pick them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And what were the weather conditions on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: The weather was awful. It was raining.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And you all had to wait outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Now, when the whole group was taken to -- when the whole group was there at Sovicka Vrata, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Then they put us on eight buses, two trucks with canvas cover, and in the night, at 21.50, we left Sovicka Vrata. We went across a mountain in the direction of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And what were the conditions in the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Did you have -- did you have your baby at the bus as well, I presume.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And what happened to her during that ride?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: As the road was bad, it was a mountain track and there were a lot of holes along the way, and the bus was bumping up and down, and my baby jumped out of my hands. So that fell out of my hands. So that --

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Did she --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: -- that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: Did she suffer an injury from that?

utterances.speaker: MS. LASAN
utterances.text: And was it treated successfully?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C
utterances.text: Thank God, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm almost done with my examination-in-chief, but just for the last couple of questions, I would like to go into private session, if that's okay, Mr. Fourmy.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two minutes and thirty-five seconds on the outside, Mr. Prosecutor. I'm joking, of course. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
